questions.q: A straight line is $36$cm long. Points are to be marked on the line from both the ends so that the first point is at a distance of $1$cm from one end, the second point is at a distance of $2$cm from the first point, the third point is at a distance of $3$cm from the second point, and so on. If the points at the ends are not counted, and the common points are counted as one, then what is the number of points?
questions.solution:
Upon analysing& the distances and the points from the given question, we can form the following table:

From the first end& & & From the second end
Point&

Distance

(From 1st end)

 Point& & &

Distance

(From 2nd& end)
First $1$~cm First $35$~cm
Second $3$~cm Second $33$~cm
Third $6$~cm Third $30$~cm
Fourth $10$~cm Fourth $26$~cm
Fifth $15$~cm Fifth $21$~cm
Sixth $21$~cm Sixth $15$~cm
Seventh $28$~cm Seventh $8$~cm
Eighth $36$~cm Eighth $0$~cm

The points~at $0$~cm and $36$~cm are endpoints. Hence, these two points are excluded.~

The four points at $15$~cm and $21$~cm are common points. Hence, two of these are also excluded.

Therefore, the required number of points~
$= 16 - 4 = 12$.

Hence, the correct answer is~$12 .$

questions.q: The sum of present ages of 3 persons is 72 yrs. Seven years ago, their ages were in the ratio \(4: 6: 7\). What are their present ages in years?
questions.solution: Given: The sum of present ages of 3 persons \(=72\) years Seven years ago, their ages were in the ratio \(4: 6: 7\) Formula Used: Sum of present ages \(=x+y+z\) Ratio relation: \((x-7):(y-7):(z-7)=4: 6: 7\) Calculation: Let the ages of three persons seven years ago be \(4 $\mathrm{k},$6 $\mathrm{k}$\), and 7 k respectively. Then, their present ages are \((4 k+7),(6 k+7)\), and \((7 k+7)\). According to the given condition: \(\begin{aligned} & (4 $\mathrm{k}+$7)+(6 $\mathrm{k}+$7)+(7 $\mathrm{k}+$7)=72 \\ & \Rightarrow 4 $\mathrm{k}+$6 $\mathrm{k}+$7 $\mathrm{k}+$21=72 \\ & \Rightarrow 17 $\mathrm{k}+$21=72 \\ & \Rightarrow 17 $\mathrm{k}=$72-21 \\ & \Rightarrow 17 $\mathrm{k}=$51 \\ & \Rightarrow $\mathrm{k}=$51 / 17 \\ & \Rightarrow $\mathrm{k}=$3 \end{aligned}\) So, their present ages are: \(4 $\mathrm{k}+$7=4 \times 3+7=12+7=19\) years \(6 k+7=6 \times 3+7=18+7=25\) years \(7 k+7=7 \times 3+7=21+7=28\) years The present ages are 19, 25, and 28 years.
questions.source: English and Logical Reasoning Prep Guide

questions.q: There are some cows, bulls, and $45$ hens in a group. One caretaker looks after $15$ animals. The number of bulls is twice the number of cows. If the number of the head is less than the total number of feet by $186$ (including the caretaker), then how many caretakers are there?
questions.solution:
Let the number& of cows $=$~$x$

So, the number of bulls $=$~$2x$

Number of hens $=45$
Number of caretakers required $=$~$\dfrac{x + 2x + 45}{15}$
Number of feet $=$

(Number~of~feet~of& cow) $\times$ (Number~of~cows) $+$~(Number~of~feet& of& bull $\times$ (Number~of~bulls) $+$(Number~of~feet~of& hen) $\times$~(Number~of~hens)& $+$(Number~of~feet~of& caretaker) $\times$ (Number~of~caretakers)~

$=$~$4x + 8x + 90 + 2 ( \dfrac{x + 2x + 45}{15} )$
Number of head $=$~(Number~of~head& of& cow) $\times$ (Number~of~cows) $+$(Number~of~head~of& bull $\times$~(Number~of~bulls) $+$(Number~of~head~of& hen) $\times$ (Number~of~hens) $+$(Number~of~head~of& caretaker) $\times$ (Number~of~caretakers)~

$=$~$x + 2x + 45 + \dfrac{x + 2x + 45}{15}$

Since, $4x + 8x + 90 + 2\left(\dfrac{x + 2x + 45}{15}\right) - \left(x + 2x + 45 + \dfrac{x + 2x + 45}{15}\right) = 186$
~ ~$9x + 45 + \dfrac{x + 2x + 45}{15} = 186$

$9x + \dfrac{x + 2x + 45}{15} = 141$

$138x = 2115 - 45$

$x = \dfrac{2070}{138} = 15$
~ ~ ~ &
Number of caretakers $=\dfrac{x + 2x + 45}{15} = \dfrac{15 + 2 \times 15 + 45}{15} = \dfrac{90}{15} = 6$

Hence, the number of caretakers is $6$.
questions.source: English and Logical Reasoning Prep Guide

questions.q: $A$ is half as old as $B . C$ is twice as old as $B$. How many times is $C$ as old as $A ?$
questions.solution:
According to the question,

$A$ is half as old as $B$ that means,

~$\dfrac{1}{2}B = A$~... ($1$)

$C$~is twice as old as $B$,

$C = 2B$~... ($2$)

Compare eq. ($1$)~and ($2$), we get

$2A = \dfrac{C}{2}$

$4A = C$

Hence, $C$ is $4$ times older than $A$.

questions.q: A is $4$ times as heavy as B. B is half the weight of C. C is $2 . 5$ times as heavy as D. D is one fourth the weight of E. Who is the heaviest?
questions.solution:
According to the question,

A $= 4$B

B $= \dfrac{C}{2}$

C $= 2 . 5 \times$D

D $= \dfrac{1}{4} \times$E

A : B $= 4: 1 = 20: 5$

B : C $= 1: 2 = 5: 10$

C : D $= 5: 2 = 10: 4$

D : E $= 1: 4 = 4: 16$

So,

A : B : C : D : E $= 20: 5: 10: 4: 16$

From this ratio, it is clear that A is the heaviest.

questions.q: The average of nine numbers is 60, that of the first five numbers is 55 and the next three is 65. The ninth number is 10 less than the tenth number. Then, tenth number is -
questions.solution: Given: Average of nine numbers \(=60\) Average of first five numbers \(=55\) and average of next three numbers \(=65\) Tenth number \(=\) Ninth number +10 Concept used: Average \(=\) Total sum of all numbers \(/\) (Count of the numbers) Calculation: The sum of nine numbers \(=60 \times 9=540\) The sum of the first five numbers \(=55 \times 5=275\) The sum of the next three numbers \(=65 \times 3=195\) Ninth number \(=(540-275-195)=(540-470)=70\) \(\therefore\) Tenth number \(=70+10=80\)
questions.source: English and Logical Reasoning Prep Guide

Read the following graph carefully and answer the question given below:
Ratio of import and export of a company in different years



If import and export are increased by& $20 %$~and $10 %$~respectively in $2001$, the resultant export became $₹ 50000$. What was the import in that year?
questions.solution:
From the graph, it is clear that the ratio of import& \left(I\right)$~and export \left(E\right)$~in the year~$2001$~is~$6 . 5$~i.e.

$\dfrac{I}{E} = 6 . 5 - \left(1\right)$

Increased export,~${E}_{1} = E + $\dfrac{10}{100}$E = $\dfrac{11}{10}$E$

Increased import,~${I}_{1} = I + $\dfrac{20}{100}$I = $\dfrac{12}{10}$I$

Increased export, ${E}_{1} = ₹ 50000$

So,

\dfrac{11}{10}$E = 50000E = $\dfrac{50000 \times 10}{11}$E = ₹ 45454 . 55$

Using the given ratio of import and export and the increased import~we get,

\dfrac{\dfrac{12}{10}{I}_{1}}{45454 . 55} =$6 . 5{I}_{1} = $\dfrac{6 . 5 \times 45454 . 55 \times 10}{12}{I}_{1} =$₹ 246212 . 15$

Hence, the required import~$= ₹ 246212 . 15

$

questions.q: The batting average for 27 innings of a cricket player is 47 runs. His highest score in an innings exceeds his lowest score by 157 runs. If these two innings are excluded, the average score of the remaining 25 innings is 42 runs. Find his highest score in an innings.
questions.solution: Given: The batting average for 27 innings of a cricket player is 47 runs. His highest score exceeds his lowest score by 157 runs. If these two innings are excluded, the average of the remaining 25 innings is 42 runs. Formula used: Average run \(=\) Total run in total innings/Total number of innings Calculation: Sum of runs for 27 innings of a cricket player \(=47 \times 27=1269\) Sum of runs for 25 innings of a cricket player \(=42 \times 25=1050\) Sum of remaining 2 innings \(=1269-1050=219\) Let the minimum score be \(x\) and the maximum score be \(x+157\) According to the question, \(\begin{aligned} & x+x+157=219 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 x=219-157 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 x=62 \\ & \Rightarrow x=31 \end{aligned}\) So, highest score \(=157+31\) \(\Rightarrow 188\) \(\therefore\) His highest score in an innings is 188.
questions.source: English and Logical Reasoning Prep Guide

questions.q: An elevator has a capacity of $12$~adults or $20$~children. How many adults can board the elevator with $15$& children?<gwmw style="display:none;"></gwmw>
questions.solution:
As per the question :

Let the weight of one adult & $= x$

And the weight of one child ~$= y$

Then, total capacity $= 12 \times x = 20 \times y$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{3x}{5}$~

Let $A$ be the number of adults that board the elevator with $15$ children.

According to the question :~

$15y + Ax = 12x$
~
$15 \times \dfrac{3x}{5} + A \times x = 12 \times x$

$⇒ 9x + Ax = 12x$

$⇒ 9 + A = 12$

$⇒ A = 3$

Hence, $3$ adults can board the elevator with $15$ children.

questions.q: An enterprising businessman earns an income of $₹ 1$ on the first day of his business. On every subsequent day, he earns an income which is just double of that made on the previous day. On the ${10}^{th}$day of business, his income is:
questions.solution:
Given, income on the first day& $= ₹ 1$

Again, income on the second~day~$= ₹ 1 \times 2 = ₹ {2}^{1}$

Now, income on the third day~$= ₹ 2 \times ₹ {2}^{1}$

$= ₹ {2}^{2}$and so on.

Therefore, income on the nth day~$= ₹ {2}^{n - 1}$

So, income on the 10th day $= ₹ {2}^{10 - 1} = ₹ {2}^{9}$

Hence, $₹ {2}^{9}$& is the correct answer.

questions.q: To succeed in a competition, Jermilin requires an average score of 75 in four exams. His score in the first three exams is 78, 74 and 70. How many scores should he get in the fourth test to succeed in the competition?
questions.solution: Given: Jermilin's scores in the first three exams: 78, 74, 70 The average score required in all four exams: 75 Let x be the score Jermilin needs to get in the fourth exam to achieve an average score of 75. Formula: Average score \(=\) (sum of all scores) \(/\) (number of scores) Calculation: We can use this formula to solve for x : \(75=(78+74+70+x) / 4\) Multiplying both sides by 4 : \(300=222+x\) Subtracting 222 from both sides: \(x=78\) Therefore, Jermilin needs to score 78 in the fourth exam to achieve an average score of 75 in all four exams. \(\therefore\) Option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.q: The average weight of P and his three friends is 55 kg. If P is 4 kg more than the average weight of his three friends, what is P's weight (in kg)?
questions.solution: Given: The average weight of \(P\) and his three friends \(=55 $\mathrm{~kg}$\) The weight of \(P=4 $\mathrm{~kg}$\) more than the average weight of his three friends Formula used: The total sum of the terms \(=\) Average \($\times$\) Number of terms Calculation: The total weight of \(P\) and his three friends \(=55 $\times$4=220 $\mathrm{~kg}$\) Let, the average weight of three friends \(=x\) So, the total weight of three friends \(=3 x\) The weight of \(P=x+4\) Then, \((x+4)+3 x=220\) \(\Rightarrow 4 x+4=220\) \(\Rightarrow 4 $\mathrm{x}=$220-4=216\) \(\Rightarrow x=216 / 4=54\) \(\therefore\) P's weight \(=4+54=58 $\mathrm{~kg}$\) \(\therefore\) The P's weight (in kg) is 58 kg

questions.q: Seven years from now, Anamika will be as old as Malini was 4 years ago. Srinidhi was born 2 years ago. The average age of Anamika, Malini and Srinidhi 10 years from now will be 33 years. What is the present age of Anamika?
questions.solution: Let the present age of Anamika be \(A\), Malini be \(M\) and that of Srinidhi be \(S\). The, according to the question: 1) Seven years from now, Anamika will be as old as Malini was 4 years ago. \(\begin{aligned} & A+7=M-4 \\ & \Rightarrow M=A+11 \\ & S=2 $\text { years } \end{aligned}$\) And, 2) Srinidhi was born 2 years ago. The average age of Anamika, Malini and Srinidhi 10 years from now will be 33 years. \(\begin{aligned} & $\frac{(A+10+M+10+S+10)}{3}=$33 \\ & A+M+S+30=33 \times 3 \\ & A+M+S=99-30 \\ & A+M+S=69 \end{aligned}\) Now, by substituting the above values, \(\begin{aligned} & A+(A+11)+2=69 \\ & 2 A+13=69 \\ & A=56 \div 2 \end{aligned}\) \$(\mathrm{A}=$28 $\text { years }$\) Hence, the present age of Anamika is \(28\) years is the correct answer.$

questions.q: Ages of father and son add up to 50. Six years back father's age was 6 more than thrice his son's age. What will be the father's age 6 years hence?
questions.solution: Let the age of father be F and that of son be S . \(\begin{aligned} \text{ and } F+S=50 $\text { (Given) }$\\ \text{ and } S=50-F \quad ...(i) \end{aligned}\) Six years back father's age was 6 more than thrice his son's age. According to problem: \((F-6)=3(S-6)+6\) ...(ii) Substituting the value of equation (i) in (ii), we get: \$(\begin{aligned}$& F-6=3(50-F-6)+6 \\ & \Rightarrow F-6=3(44-F)+6 \\ & \Rightarrow F-6=132-3 F+6 \\ & \Rightarrow F+3 F=132+6+6 \\ & \Rightarrow 4 F=144 \\ & \Rightarrow F=144 / 4 \\ & \Rightarrow F=36 \end{aligned}\) So, father's age 6 years hence \(=(36+6)=42\) Hence, ' 42 ' is the correct answer.$

Then,

Age of W~$= a - 9$~years

Age of V~$= a - 9 + 3 = a - 6$~years

Age of~U $= a - 6 - 8 = a - 14$~years

Age of~T~$= a - 14 + 5 = a - 9$& years

It is clear from& above& that the ages of W& and T& are the same.

questions.solution: Given: Amita's father was 38 years old when she was born. Her mother was 36 years old when her brother was born. Her brother was four years younger than her. Calculation: Let the present age of Amita be \(P\) years. So, The age of her father \(=(38+P)\) years The age of her brother \(=(P-4)\) years The age of her mother \(=36+(P-4)=(32+P)\) years Now, the age difference between her parents \(=(38+P)-(32+P)=6\) years \(\therefore\) The difference between the ages of her parents is 6 years.

questions.q: Mr. Star was a consistent batsman throughout his career. He played 80 innings before he retired. Had he scored 10 runs in his last innings, his average would have been 50. However, in his last innings, he was dismissed for 2 runs. What was his average at the end of the 79th innings?
questions.solution: It is given that had he scored 10 runs in the last innings, his average would have been 50 . \(\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow $\frac{\text { Total runs scored }+10}{80}=$50 \\ & \Rightarrow R+10=80 \times 50 \\ & \Rightarrow R+10=4000 \\ & \Rightarrow R=4000-10=3990 \end{aligned}\) When he scored 2 runs in the last innings, the total runs scored in the first 79 innings was: \(\Rightarrow R_{79 $\text { innings }}=3990-2=3988\) Average after 79 innings: \(\Rightarrow $\text { Average }=\frac{\text { Total runs scored }}{\text { Total innings played }}=\frac{3988}{79}$\) On dividing: \(\Rightarrow $\text { Average }}=49+\frac{74}{79}\) \(\therefore\) The average at the end of the 79th innings is: \(49 $\frac{74}{79}$\)
questions.source: English and Logical Reasoning Prep Guide

questions.q:
Six boys A, B, C, D, E, and F play a game of Cards. Each has a pack of $10$ Cards. F borrows $2$ Cards from A, and gives away $5$ to C, who gives $3$ to B, while B gives $6$ to D, who passes on $1$ to E. How many Cards D has?

(A) $9$ (B) $8$

(C) $11$ (D) $15$
questions.solution: Total no. of cards with D $=$ No. of cards he is having in the beginning $+$ cards borrowed from someone else $-$ cards passed on to someone else $= 10 + 6 - 1 = 15$

questions.q: Weight of& $A$~is twice that of~$B$. Weight of~$B$ is half that of~$C$. Weight of~$C$ is~$3$ times that of~$E$. Weight of~$E$ is half that of~$D$. Who is the heaviest?
questions.solution:
Let the weight of& $D$ be~$4x$

Therefore, weight of $E$~$= \dfrac{D}{2} = \dfrac{4x}{2} = 2x$

Similarly, weight of $C$~$= 3E = 3 \times 2x = 6x$

And, weight of $B$~$= \dfrac{C}{2} = \dfrac{6x}{2} = 3x$

Therefore, weight of $A$~$= 2B = 2 \times 3x = 6x$

Thus, both $A$~and~$C$ are the heaviest.

Study the given graph and answer the following questions.

An International agency surveyed the performance of cars.

The Points are given on the basis of the following features

The points earned by Hyundai on the basis of comfort are what percent more/less than the points earned by Siena on the basis of ride/handle?
questions.solution:
The points earned by Hyundai on the basis of comfort

$= \dfrac{( 650 \times 14 )}{100}$

$= \dfrac{9100}{100}$

$= 91$

The points earned by Siena on the basis of ride/handle

$= \dfrac{( 600 \times 18 )}{100}$

$= \dfrac{10800}{100}$

$= 108$

Now, the required percentage is

$= \dfrac{( 108 - 91 )}{108} \times 100$

$= \left(\dfrac{17}{108}\right) \times 100$

$= 15 . 74 %$

questions.q: A man wears socks of two colours - black and brown. He has altogether 20 brown socks in a drawer. Supposing he has to take out the socks in the dark, how many must he take out to be sure that he has a matching pair.
questions.solution:
It is given that he has socks of 2 colours& only.

It is obvious that if he only takes out one sock then he can’t have a matching pair (since by definition a pair is 2 socks).

If he takes out 2 socks, he could select 2 that are the same colour, but he could also select one of each colour — which is not a matching pair. Therefore, 2 socks are not enough to& guarantee& that he will have a matching pair

If he takes out 3 socks then there are 2 scenarios — the first being that the first two socks he selects are matching. The second is that the first two socks he picks don’t match (without loss of generality we can assume the first is black& and the second is brown) - in this case, the next sock he selects must make a pair, since if it is black it will make a pair with the first sock, and if it is brown it will make a pair with the second sock.

Thus, we have shown that 3 socks will guarantee a pair.&
questions.source: English and Logical Reasoning Prep Guide

questions.q: A, B, C, D and E play a game of cards. A says to B, “If you give me three cards, you will have as many as E has and if I give you three cards, you will have as many as D has.” A and B together have 10 cards more than what D and E together have. If B has two cards more than what C has and the total number of cards is 133, how many cards does B have?
questions.solution:
According to the given information,

$B - 3 = E$~--------$( 1 )$
$B + 3 = D$~-------$( 2 )$
$A + B = D + E + 10$~-----$( 3 )$
$B = C + 2$~--------$( 4 )$
$A + B + C + D + E = 133$~------$( 5 )$

Now, if we add~equations~$( 1 )$~and $( 2 )$, we get,
$2B = E + D$~--------$( 6 )$

Substituting equation~$( 6 )$~in~$( 3 )$,

$A + B = 2B + 10$~ ~
$A = B + 10$~--------$( 7 )$

Substituting equations~$( 4 ) , ( 6 )$~and~$( 7 )$,~in equation~$( 5 )$, we get,

$( B + 10 ) + B + ( B - 2 ) + 2B = 133$

$5B + 8 = 133$

$5B = 125$

$B = 25$

Therefore, B has~$25$& cards.
questions.source: English and Logical Reasoning Prep Guide

Which of the graphs below best represents this relationship?
questions.solution:
According to the formula of square,

Area of square$= a^{2}$~

Where $a$~is equal to side length,

It means area of a square is directly proportional to its side length,

$Areaofsquare\alpha{( length )}^{2}$

It means if the length is zero, the area will also be zero as the curve will be reprsented by,~$y = x^{2}$.

So the~curve will start from the origin. Hence, the correct answer is option $2$.

The bar graph given below shows the sales of books (in a thousand number) from six branches of a publishing company during two consecutive years $2000$ and $2001 .$
Sales of Books (in a thousand numbers) from Six Branches - $B1, B2, B3, B4, B5$ and$B6$ of a publishing Company in $2000$ and $2001 .$


Total sales of branches$B1, B3$ and $B5$ together for both the years (in thousand numbers) is ______.
questions.solution:
Total sales of branches $B1 = ( 80 + 105 ) = 185$

Total sales of branches~$B3 = ( 95 + 110 ) = 205$

Total sales of branches $B5 =( 75 + 95 ) = 170$
Total sales~$= 185 + 205 + 170 = 560$
Hence, the total sales is~$560$.

questions.q: Find out the number of people who do not play any game?
questions.solution:
As given in the Venn diagram, $25$plays cricket, $22$ plays tennis and $16$ plays both.
The number of people who play only cricket is $25 - 16 = 9$
The number of people who play only tennis is $22 - 16 = 6$
So, people who do not play any game are,
$⇒ 40 - ( 6 + 9 + 16 )$
$⇒ 40 - 31$
$⇒ 9$
Hence, option A is the correct answer.

questions.q: The average age of a group of 25 boys is 17 years. If one boy leaves the group, the average age becomes 17.2 years. What is the age of the boy who left the group?
questions.solution:
Given: The average age of a group of 25 boys is 17 years. If one boy leaves the group, the average age becomes 17.2 years. We need to find the age of the boy who left the group. Solution:
Calculate the total age of all 25 boys. Average age of 25 boys \(=17\) years Total age of 25 boys \(=25 \times 17=425\) years
Calculate the total age of 24 boys after one leaves. New average age of 24 boys \(=17.2\) years Total age of 24 boys \(=24 \times 17.2=412.8\) years
Find the age of the boy who left the group. Age of the boy who left \(=\) Total age of 25 boys - Total age of 24 boys Age of the boy who left \(=425-412.8=12.2\) years Conclusion: The age of the boy who left the group is \(12.2\) years.
questions.source: English and Logical Reasoning Prep Guide
